content:
After releasing the public beta versions of macOS 27, iPadOS 27, iOS 27, and other updates unveiled at WWDC26 yesterday, Apple is now rolling out the first public beta firmware for the AirPods Max 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and AirPods (4th generation). Here's what you need to know.

The first AirPods public beta firmware is now available

Apple announced several new AirPods features at last month's WWDC26 that will arrive alongside iOS 27 and other upcoming operating system updates.

These include customisable EQ sound settings, allowing users to personalise their AirPods listening experience, as well as expanded GymKit support, enabling AirPods Pro 3 users to sync heart rate data via iPhone.

Apple is also rolling out beta firmware for the AirPods Max 2 for the first time. Users can enrol in the beta programme through a device running iOS 27 or macOS 27.

Following yesterday's release of the first public beta versions of iOS 27 and Apple's other upcoming operating systems, the company has now released the first public beta firmware update for the following AirPods models:

  • AirPods Max 2
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2
  • AirPods Pro 2 (USB-C)
  • AirPods (4th generation)
  • AirPods (4th generation, Active Noise Cancellation)

AirPods firmware version 9.0.314 has a release number of 9A5314b, matching last week's developer beta.

Installing AirPods Beta Firmware

Here's Apple's official guide on how to enrol eligible AirPods in the firmware beta programme:

Enable Beta Updates — For Macs running macOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your Mac via Bluetooth settings. Go to System Settings > Bluetooth, then click the (i) next to your AirPods. In the AirPods settings menu, scroll down to find "AirPods Beta Updates." Use the toggle to enable beta software updates. For iPhone and iPad running iOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your iOS device. Go to Settings > Bluetooth, then tap the (i) next to your AirPods. Apple notes that once users toggle on "AirPods Beta Updates," "the firmware update will install automatically when the AirPods are in the charging case and near a paired iPhone or Mac."
